title: Why take part?
text: Teams learn by doing, and leave with skills, friendships and projects that keep making an impact. Solve real problems Work on challenges that matter in your own school and community, and measure the difference you make. Learn from experts Get feedback from scientists, engineers and entrepreneurs, and connect with students in more than 60 countries. Win grants and recognition Medals in every category, certificates for all teams, and grants of up to €5,000 to bring winning ideas to life.

title: Six challenges, one planet
text: Every team chooses one category. Each comes with a practical brief for 2027. Renewable Energy Design ways to generate, store or save clean energy in your school and community. Waste Reduction & Circular Economy Rethink how products are made, used and reused so less ends up in landfill. Sustainable Design & Architecture Create products, buildings and public spaces that do more with less. Climate Solutions Measure, communicate and act on climate change, locally and globally. Water & Oceans Protect fresh water and marine life through smart monitoring and conservation. Biodiversity & Food Systems Grow food sustainably and give nature space to thrive. See all challenges and briefs

title: How it works
text: Register your team Form a team of 2–5 students with a mentor and choose a challenge. Round 1: Knowledge Challenge Take a 90-minute online quiz on sustainability science from your school. Round 2: Project Challenge Spend four weeks building, testing and documenting a real solution. Global Finals Present your project to an international jury in Lisbon or online.

title: About
text: Home About About the Olympiad Since 2020, the Sustainable Olympiad has brought students together to compete, collaborate and innovate for a healthier planet.

title: Our mission
text: We believe the people who will live longest with the consequences of today's environmental choices deserve the tools, knowledge and platform to shape them. The Sustainable Olympiad is a non-profit, international competition for students aged 12 to 25. Teams investigate an environmental problem in their own community, design a solution, test it and share what they learn, guided by mentors and assessed by experts. Unlike traditional olympiads, success is not only about knowing the right answer. It is about making a measurable difference and inspiring others to follow. “We started with a question about our cafeteria bins. We finished with a product that a local cooperative now makes every week.” Planet Award winning team, 2026

title: Our goals
text: Inspire action Turn concern about the environment into practical, measurable projects. Build skills Develop scientific thinking, creativity, teamwork and communication. Connect communities Link students, schools, researchers and businesses across borders. Include everyone Keep participation free, accessible and open to every school.

title: Our values
text: Evidence over opinion. We value honest data, including results that did not go to plan. Collaboration over competition. Teams compete, but every project and every lesson is shared openly. Access for all. No fees, low-cost materials, travel support and full accessibility. Practise what we teach. Our Finals are low-waste, mostly plant-based and carbon-accounted.

title: Our history
text: From an online experiment during school closures to a global community. 2020 The first Olympiad Three science teachers launch an online challenge for 40 teams from 14 countries during school closures. 2021 Going global A free mentor programme opens, and participation triples to 120 teams. 2022 First in-person Finals Finalists meet in Lisbon, and the University division is introduced. 2023 Open Planet Foundation joins Student grants of up to €5,000 help winning teams turn prototypes into real projects. 2024 Accessibility first Captioned sessions, screen-reader-compatible quizzes and travel support become standard. 2025 Climate Solutions category A record 280 teams compete, with a new category focused on climate data and adaptation. 2026 Sixth edition Students from 62 countries take part; the winning team turns cafeteria waste into bioplastic.

title: Our impact so far
text: 6 editions held 62 countries 4,800+ students 1,150 projects submitted

title: Who organises the Olympiad
text: The Olympiad is run by an independent non-profit association of educators and scientists, supported by volunteers from universities and partner organisations. An advisory board of teachers, students and accessibility specialists reviews the rules and challenges every year. Judges are recruited openly and declare any conflicts of interest. Our accounts are published every year after the Finals.

title: The six categories
text: Every category is open to all three divisions. Briefs are deliberately open, so you can adapt them to your local context.

title: Renewable Energy
text: Design ways to generate, store or save clean energy in your school and community. Teams investigate how communities can move away from fossil fuels. Projects may range from a solar-powered phone charging station to an energy audit that cuts a school's electricity bill. 2027 challenge brief Reduce your school's energy use by at least 15% using low-cost, renewable or efficiency-based measures. Example projects Small-scale solar, wind or micro-hydro prototypes Energy audits and behaviour-change campaigns Low-cost thermal insulation or passive cooling Useful skills Physics, engineering, data analysis Register for this challenge : Renewable Energy

title: Waste Reduction & Circular Economy
text: Rethink how products are made, used and reused so less ends up in landfill. Teams tackle the full life cycle of materials, from reducing single-use plastics to turning food waste into compost, biogas or new products. 2027 challenge brief Cut the waste your school or neighbourhood sends to landfill and show measurable results over four weeks. Example projects Composting and food-waste recovery systems Repair cafés, swap shops and reuse schemes Biodegradable or upcycled materials Useful skills Chemistry, biology, entrepreneurship Register for this challenge : Waste Reduction & Circular Economy

title: Sustainable Design & Architecture
text: Create products, buildings and public spaces that do more with less. Teams apply eco-design principles to everyday objects, buildings or neighbourhoods, considering materials, energy, water and the wellbeing of the people who use them. 2027 challenge brief Redesign one space or product in your community so that it uses fewer resources and serves people better. Example projects Green roofs, shading and natural ventilation Products designed for repair and disassembly Accessible, low-carbon public spaces Useful skills Design, mathematics, art, technology Register for this challenge : Sustainable Design & Architecture

title: Climate Solutions
text: Measure, communicate and act on climate change, locally and globally. Teams develop tools, campaigns or policy proposals that reduce emissions or help communities adapt to a changing climate, backed by sound data. 2027 challenge brief Calculate a real carbon footprint in your community and propose a credible plan to reduce it. Example projects Carbon calculators and climate data dashboards Flood, heat or drought adaptation plans Climate communication and advocacy campaigns Useful skills Geography, statistics, communication Register for this challenge : Climate Solutions

title: Water & Oceans New
text: Protect fresh water and marine life through smart monitoring and conservation. New for 2027. Teams explore water scarcity, pollution and ocean health, building solutions that save, clean or protect water resources. 2027 challenge brief Monitor a local water source for one month and design an intervention that improves its quality or reduces its use. Example projects Low-cost water quality sensors Rainwater harvesting and grey-water reuse Beach and river clean-up data projects Useful skills Biology, chemistry, electronics Register for this challenge : Water & Oceans

title: Biodiversity & Food Systems
text: Grow food sustainably and give nature space to thrive. Teams work on pollinator habitats, school gardens, urban farming or reducing the footprint of what we eat, combining field observation with practical action. 2027 challenge brief Increase biodiversity on your school grounds and document the change with a species survey. Example projects Pollinator gardens and wildlife corridors Hydroponics and vertical farming Low-impact school menus Useful skills Biology, ecology, nutrition Register for this challenge : Biodiversity & Food Systems

Innovation 25% Is the idea original, or does it apply an existing idea in a new way? Feasibility 20% Could the solution realistically be built, funded and scaled? title: Rulebook contents
text: 1. Eligibility 2. Teams and mentors 3. Registration 4. Competition format 5. Project submissions 6. Judging 7. Academic integrity 8. Safety and ethics 9. Code of conduct 10. Accessibility and reasonable adjustments 11. Intellectual property and media 12. Prizes

title: 1. Eligibility
text: The Olympiad is open to students aged 12 to 25 who are enrolled in a school, college or university during the 2026–27 academic year. Junior division: students aged 12–14 on 1 September 2026. Senior division: students aged 15–18 on 1 September 2026. University division: undergraduate students aged 18–25. A team competes in the division of its oldest member.

title: 2. Teams and mentors
text: Each team has 2 to 5 students and one supervising mentor aged 21 or over, normally a teacher or lecturer. Students may belong to only one team per edition. A mentor may supervise up to three teams. Mentors guide and support, but the work must be done by the students. Team members can be replaced until the Round 1 start date by contacting the organisers.

title: 3. Registration
text: Registration is free and is completed online by the team captain before the registration deadline. Each team chooses one category when registering. The category can be changed until Round 1 starts. For students under 18, the mentor confirms that parental or guardian consent has been obtained. Schools may register more than one team.

title: 4. Competition format
text: The Olympiad has three stages. Teams that do not advance still receive written feedback and a certificate of participation. Round 1, Online Knowledge Challenge: a 90-minute multiple-choice and short-answer quiz taken together as a team. Round 2, Project Challenge: four weeks to build and test a solution to the category brief, with a report of up to 3,000 words and a three-minute video. Global Finals: a ten-minute presentation and a ten-minute question-and-answer session with the jury, in person or online.

title: 5. Project submissions
text: Round 2 submissions are uploaded through the participant portal before 23:59 Lisbon time on the deadline date. Reports are submitted as PDF and videos as MP4 or a public video link. Videos must include captions, and reports must use headings and alt text for images. All sources, data sets and tools, including AI tools, must be credited. Late submissions are accepted only in documented emergencies.

title: 6. Judging
text: Projects are scored by an independent jury of scientists, educators, engineers and entrepreneurs. Each project is reviewed by at least three judges. Environmental impact: 30% Innovation: 25% Feasibility: 20% Scientific rigour: 15% Communication: 10% Judges declare any conflict of interest and do not score teams from their own institution. The jury's decisions are final.

title: 7. Academic integrity
text: Teams must submit their own original work. Plagiarism, data fabrication or undisclosed outside help leads to disqualification. AI tools may be used for research and editing, provided their use is described in the report. Projects must not have won another international competition before.

title: 8. Safety and ethics
text: Experiments must be carried out safely and under adult supervision where needed. No project may harm people, animals or ecosystems. Research with human participants requires informed consent and must protect their privacy. Mains electricity, hazardous chemicals and power tools may be used only under a mentor's supervision.

title: 9. Code of conduct
text: The Olympiad is an inclusive community. Participants, mentors, judges and volunteers treat each other with respect. Harassment and discrimination of any kind are not tolerated. Concerns can be reported confidentially to the organisers at any time.

title: 10. Accessibility and reasonable adjustments
text: We want everyone to be able to take part. Teams can request adjustments such as extra time, screen-reader-compatible quiz formats, sign language interpretation or step-free venue access. Request adjustments in the registration form or by contacting us at least two weeks before the relevant round.

title: 11. Intellectual property and media
text: Teams keep full ownership of their ideas and projects. By entering, teams allow the organisers to share project summaries, photos and videos to promote the Olympiad, with credit. Teams may opt out of photography at the Finals.

title: 12. Prizes
text: Gold, silver and bronze medals are awarded in each category and division. The Planet Award goes to the best project overall. Winning teams receive grants of up to €5,000 to develop their project further. All finalists receive certificates and mentoring from our partners.

title: Participant guidelines
text: Practical advice for every stage of the competition. Before you register Form a team of 2–5 students with a mix of skills: science, design, writing and presenting. Find a mentor, usually a teacher, who can meet with you regularly. Read the rulebook and choose the category that excites your team most. Preparing for Round 1 Review the sustainability topics in the study guide on our Resources page. Practise with past quizzes and agree how your team will divide questions. Test your internet connection and device the day before. Running your project in Round 2 Start with a clear problem statement and measure your baseline before you change anything. Keep a project log with dates, data, photos and decisions. Involve your community: interview the people affected by the problem. Make your report and video accessible, with headings, alt text and captions. Presenting at the Finals Tell a story: the problem, what you tried, what you measured and what you learned. Show real evidence. Judges value honest results, including failures. Rehearse answering questions and share speaking time across the team.

title: Sustainability tips
text: Small everyday actions for students, schools and families. Energy Switch off lights, screens and chargers when you leave a room. Use daylight where you can and choose LED bulbs. Lower the heating by 1 °C. It can cut heating energy use by up to 10%. Waste Carry a reusable bottle, cup and lunch box. Repair, swap or donate before you throw away. Sort your recycling correctly. A contaminated bin can end up in landfill. Water Take shorter showers and turn the tap off while brushing your teeth. Collect rainwater for plants. Report leaking taps and pipes at school. Food Plan meals and use leftovers to reduce food waste. Eat more seasonal, local and plant-based food. Compost fruit and vegetable scraps. Transport Walk, cycle, scoot or take public transport where you can. Share rides for longer journeys. Choose video calls when travelling is not necessary. Nature Plant native flowers for pollinators. Leave a wild corner in gardens and school grounds. Join or organise a local clean-up.

title: FAQ
text: Home FAQ Frequently Asked Questions Quick answers about taking part. Can’t find what you need? Contact us. Filter questions Type a word such as “team”, “cost” or “travel”. Expand all answers

title: General
text: What is the Sustainable Olympiad? An international competition where student teams develop real solutions to environmental challenges in six categories, from renewable energy to biodiversity. Learn more about us . Who can take part? Students aged 12 to 25 who are enrolled in a school, college or university. Teams compete in the Junior (12–14), Senior (15–18) or University (18–25) division. Does it cost anything to participate? No. Registration, all competition rounds and the starter resources are free. Travel support is available for in-person finalist teams. Is the competition held in English? Yes, the Olympiad is run in English. Teams may use translation tools and should mention this in their report. Judges assess ideas, not language skills.

title: Registration
text: How do I register a team? The team captain completes the online registration form before 15 January 2027. You will need the details of every team member and your mentor. Can I take part on my own? Teams need at least two students. If you cannot find teammates, contact us and we will try to match you with other students from your region. Can we change our category or team members after registering? Yes. Changes are allowed until Round 1 starts on 6 February 2027. Email us with your team name and the change. Does our mentor have to be a teacher? Usually yes, but any responsible adult aged 21 or over with a connection to your school or university can act as mentor.

title: Competition
text: Do we need to travel to compete? No. Rounds 1 and 2 take place online from your school. The Global Finals are hybrid, so finalists can present in Lisbon or online. What equipment do we need? A computer with an internet connection is enough for Round 1. For Round 2, most projects use low-cost or recycled materials. Expensive equipment does not earn extra points. Can we use AI tools? Yes, for research and editing, as long as you describe how you used them in your report. The ideas and the work must be your team's own. How are projects judged? By an independent jury using five weighted criteria: impact, innovation, feasibility, scientific rigour and communication. See the judging criteria .

title: Support & Accessibility
text: What accessibility support is available? We offer extra time, screen-reader-compatible quizzes, captioned sessions, sign language interpretation and step-free venues. Request adjustments when you register or contact us . How can my school become a partner or host an event? We would love to hear from you. Visit Partners or get in touch . How do you use our personal data? We use registration data only to run the competition, and we never sell it. Mentors confirm guardian consent for participants under 18. Data is deleted 12 months after each edition. Still have a question? Our team usually replies within two working days. Contact us

title: Accessibility Statement
text: Home Accessibility Accessibility Statement We want everyone to be able to use this website and take part in the Olympiad.

title: Our commitment
text: This website is designed to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at level AA. Accessibility is part of how we design, write and test every page.

title: Accessibility features
text: A “Skip to main content” link and clear page landmarks for screen readers. Full keyboard support, with a clearly visible focus indicator. Text and controls that meet WCAG AA colour contrast in every theme. An accessibility toolbar with text size, dark mode, high contrast, text spacing and link highlighting. Layouts that reflow at 400% zoom and on small screens without horizontal scrolling. Respect for your system’s reduced-motion and dark mode settings. Forms with visible labels, clear instructions and error messages that are announced to screen readers. Text alternatives for all meaningful images, with decorative images hidden from assistive technology.

title: Using the accessibility toolbar
text: Select Accessibility at the top of any page to open the toolbar. Your choices are remembered on this device. Text size: enlarge text up to 200%. Browser zoom (Ctrl or Cmd and +) also works. Dark mode: light text on a dark background. High contrast: maximum contrast with yellow highlights. Text spacing: more space between lines, words and letters. Highlight links: makes every link stand out clearly.

title: Known limitations
text: The downloadable PDFs are not yet fully tagged for screen readers. The same content is available as web pages on the Rules & Guidelines page. The optional schools map uses a third-party map service. The same information is always available in the list on the Partners page.

title: Feedback and contact
text: If you have difficulty using any part of this website, or you need information in a different format, please contact us . We aim to respond within two working days. This statement was last reviewed on 1 October 2026.
